prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat moire bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: After reading the whole first round I keep B031 as my preferred configuration, but with a clearer view of what it rests on. The durable result is the single-particle one: Bistritzer and MacDonald showed analytically that interlayer tunnelling flattens the lowest bands at a discrete magic angle, and the 2018 experiments by Jarillo-Herrero and colleagues found correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle. That is a quantitative, falsifiable prediction followed by a decisive experiment in one tunable material, the pattern I trust most as a theorist who checks calculations against spectra. Independent groups have since seen the correlated insulators and superconductivity (I recall groups at Columbia, Santa Barbara, Barcelona and Princeton, and the committee should confirm the exact list with the experimentalists), and the flat-band picture is supported by continuum and ab initio calculations. It is new quantum behaviour in a material and it opened a large field of moire quantum matter, in the line of the 2010 graphene prize. I also say plainly that B029 is the better-prepared ballot on reproducibility and credit, and I would not regard it as a poor outcome.
statement.case_against: The reservations of Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce are fair on three counts. Attribution: Yuan Cao, Fatemi and Dean's group are outside any three-name set, and the Bistritzer slot invites the question of why a first author of a joint prediction is credited while the lead experimental author is not. Maturity: the field is under ten years old, the pairing mechanism is open, and twist-angle disorder makes device-to-device behaviour vary. Comparison: B029 has a stable interpretation, cross-laboratory agreement at 10^-18 and a two-name credit that nobody on the committee has disputed, whereas B031 needs the committee to accept an explicit statement about whom it leaves out. If the committee decides the credit cannot be defended, the right move is B029 as the whole prize, not a weakened B031.

responses.point: Kroll accepts B031 as a striking prediction-then-experiment discovery but would be more comfortable once the interpretation has settled, and contrasts it with the lattice clock, whose interpretation has been stable for years.
responses.response: You asked me to argue that the physics is settled enough, and I can only argue it for part of the problem. The part that is settled is the one the citation names: the magic-angle flat bands and the existence of correlated insulating and superconducting states, which have been reproduced by several independent groups and match continuum and ab initio band calculations. The part that is not settled is why the system superconducts, and I would state that in the citation by honouring the observation of the phases and not an explanation of them. That is how we treated superconductors before the mechanism was understood. I still see a difference in kind from B029, which is a refinement of a measurement we already knew how to do, whereas B031 shows matter behaving in a way we did not expect. I accept that your argument from stability of interpretation is real and gives B029 an edge on maturity.

responses.point: Pearce asks whether the credited contribution is settled enough to last, whether three names can be defended given Cao, Fatemi and Dean, and says he would be convinced if condensed-matter members argue the flat-band picture is durable.
responses.response: My answer to the first question is yes for the flat-band picture and the existence of the phases, and no for the mechanism, which is why the citation should name the first two only. On the second, I cannot give you a wholly comfortable answer. The statutes allow three, and the set that tracks the prediction and the experimental discovery is MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero; the lead student and the early independent groups would be left out, as has been the case in earlier prizes, and we should say so openly in the committee's own notes. The cleaner fallback for the credit worry is a two-name pair, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, which I now consider equally defensible, and I would put the choice between two and three names to a vote and not assume it. Your chair question about independent reproduction is best settled by our experimentalists, since my knowledge of the device literature is second hand.

responses.point: Danielsson regards B031 as somewhat early, wants the credit allocation shown to be robust, and would move it up only if colleagues can show that, while keeping B016 as a mature alternative.
responses.response: I cannot show you that the allocation is beyond argument, and I will not claim it. What I can offer is the structure: the prediction (2011) and the discovery (2018) are each credited to the people whose paper established them, and the omissions are of identifiable people whose work followed or accompanied that discovery. On your own configuration I see no scientific kinship between B029 and B037 and would not give it weight; if the committee wanted two parts I would prefer to see a second part chosen for its own merit, and I share your worry that Halzen alone cannot stand for an observatory collaboration. I note that B016 remains my second alternative for the reasons you give, but I also agree with Mehlig that dropping Mele while keeping Hasan is the harder attribution choice.

responses.point: Lindroth places B029 above moire matter because the credit set is clean and the physics is understood, but says she would not be upset if the committee chose B031 once the attribution is settled.
responses.response: I take that offer seriously, and it narrows our disagreement to the credit question. I accept your point that Ludlow, Bloom, Lemonde and others complicate B029 as well, so neither ballot has a perfectly clean credit; the difference is that B029's problem is a team behind a pair, which is the usual pattern, while B031's is the omission of a named lead author. On novelty I stay where I was: I regard B029 as the end of a programme that the 2005 and 2012 prizes started, and I cannot say that to a wider public as comfortably as I could say that matter does something new in twisted graphene. That is my judgement, not a claim about your field, and I defer to you and Kroll on whether the lattice clock really is distinct from those two prizes.

responses.point: Johansson accepts the B031 prediction and the reproduced phases but qualifies maturity, and on B004 keeps Blais over Girvin while flagging a possible recusal.
responses.response: Thank you for the clear statement on maturity; my reply to you is the same as to Kroll, that the phases are established and the mechanism is not, and the citation can be worded to match. On B004 I accept your reasoning for Blais as the person who led the 2004 theory, and I withdraw my earlier suggestion that Girvin belongs in the third place; I was reading the record too loosely. I also agree that your closeness to the circuit-QED community, and the adjacency to the 2025 prize, are matters that the chair should settle before any ballot on B004, and I would support you stepping back from that candidate.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the prediction-and-experiment framing of B031 as the discovery, given that the pairing mechanism is open and the field is less than ten years old.
Whether the credit should be two names (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero) or three (adding Bistritzer), and how the omission of Cao, Fatemi and Dean's group would be explained.

The exact number of independent groups that have reproduced superconductivity and the correlated insulators at the magic angle, which I recall only from general literature and which the experimentalists should confirm.
Whether B029 should overtake B031 if the committee judges maturity and a clean credit set to be decisive; I would accept that outcome.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict. I have no personal or institutional connection to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer, nor to Katori, Ye or the other credited names on the shortlist. My DFT work on 2D materials is a scientific interest, not a reason for recusal. Johansson's flagged B004 conflict does not affect my own position.
